applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Product-architecture card informed by public steel modeling/check sources; not a public steel design rule.

claims.text: Steel modeling and analysis assumptions should be captured before design checks consume forces, moments, restraints, and member properties.
A design standard defines requirements for structural steel design, while Fraia artifacts should record which inputs, assumptions, and results were used for a specific check.
Fraia should keep design actions, check inputs, and check results separate so explanations can cite public steel behavior without presenting retrieval text as a completed code check.

limitations: This is a Fraia product policy card, not an external steel-design authority.
Public steel sources justify the need for scoped inputs and checks; Fraia's artifact names are internal vocabulary.

pages_used: Specification for Structural Steel Buildings landing page

summary: Fraia should preserve design actions, check inputs, and check results as separate artifacts so steel knowledge retrieval supports checks without masquerading as them.
title: Steel Design Action And Check Input Separation
